quotes.quote: IF the head of a nominal phrase denotes a clinical sign or symptom, a deficit or state nominalization (a state noun taking a complement introduced by “of” or “in”), or an abnormality adjective plus a pathological-process noun, AND the phrase is predicated of a disease (as a complement in a disease-characterization or causal clause, e.g., “is characterized by,” “results in,” “secondary to,” in which the disease is the subject or referent), THEN annotate the full nominal phrase, including its premodifiers and complement, as **Disease Class**.

note: Cited example is in Section 1, not 1b; quoted at line 15.
